CITY OF ALHAMBRA

  NOTICE OF REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE
  ALHAMBRA ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY
  COMMISSION
  THURSDAY, MAY 14, 2026
  6:00 p.m.

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a Regular Meeting of the Alhambra
Environmental Sustainability Commission will be held on Thursday, May 14,
2026 at 6:00 p.m. in Conference Room A, on the second floor of the Alhambra
City Hall, 111 S. First St., Alhambra, California, pursuant to the order of the
Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission Secretary.

An agenda of such regular meeting is attached hereto, incorporated herein by
reference and made a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.

  Latoya Waters,
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability
  Commission Secretary

Notice No. N2M26-64
Posted: 05/11/2026
   CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  AGENDA
  REGULAR MEETING
  ALHAMBRA ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY COMMISSION

  City Hall, 111 South First Street
  May 14, 2026
  6:00 p.m.

  I.  ROLL CALL
  Commissioner K. Chan, Commissioner S. Chan, Commissioner Gomez, Commissioner Hermosillo,
  Commissioner Scaduto

  II.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY MEETING MINUTES
  Commission Members will vote to approve April 16, 2026 meeting minutes.
  Recommended Action: Approve the meeting minutes.

  III.  SUSTAINABILITY PLAN UPDATE
  Staff will provide an update on the Sustainability Plan.
  Recommended Action: Information only. No action required

  IV.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY PLAN UPDATE DISCUSSION
  The Environmental Sustainability Commission will discuss action items for the next meeting.
  Recommended Action: Information and discussion. No action required.

  V.  PUBLIC COMMENT
  Discussion from the public of any item not specified on the agenda. Comments are welcome, but
  must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please limit
  all oral communication to five (5) minutes. Speakers must fill out a blue speaker’s card, prior to the
  meeting and submit it to the Commission Secretary. Comments must pertain to the business of the
  Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please limit all oral communications to five (5) minutes.

  VI.  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION
  Discussion from the Commission Members of any item not specified on the agenda and agenda
  items for next meeting. Items must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental
  Sustainability Commission.
  Recommended Action: Discussion only. No action required.

  VII.  ADJOURNMENT
  Adjournment to the next regular meeting on Thursday, July 9, 2026 at 6:00 p.m.

  If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and give it to
  the secretary. When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please
  make your statement as brief as possible. The maximum time for addressing the Committee is five minutes.

  If you wish to address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will be
  heard during the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Committee on a subject
  which does not appear on the agenda, but is of an environmental concern, your comments will be heard

05/14/2026
 under Public Comments. Please be advised that under the State of California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, the
Commission cannot take action on any item which does not appear on the agenda.

Copies of staff reports or other written documentation, if any, relating to each item of business described
above are on file in the Alhambra City Hall, Public Works Department, 111 S. First Street, Alhambra
California 91801 and are available for public inspection upon request during regular business hours of
7:00am to 5:30pm, Monday through Thursday.

Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior to the meeting
described herein, he or she may contact Latoya Waters, Deputy Director of Utilities, either in person at the
Utilities Department at Alhambra City Hall, 111 South First Street, or by calling via telephone at (626) 570-
5067 during regular business hours.

  MINUTES
  Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Special Meeting on April 16, 2026

The regular meeting of the Environmental Sustainability Commission was called to
order at 6:00 p.m. on April 16, 2026.

Roll Call
  Commission Members Present: Commissioner K. Chan, Commissioner S. Chan,
  Commissioner Gomez, Commissioner Hermosillo, Commissioner Scaduto

  Staff Present: Latoya Waters – Deputy Director of Utilities serving as
  Commission Secretary, Lucy Garcia – Assistant City Manager, Katie Martel –
  Management Analyst: Sustainability.

  Members of the Public:
  Sawyer Brooks

Meeting Minutes – April 16, 2026
  •  Approval of January 8, 2026 Meeting Minutes
  o Motion to approve was made and seconded (Gomez moved;
  Hermosillo seconded; support noted from K Chan and S Chan).
  o January 8, 2026 minutes approved.
  •  Sustainability Plan Update/Discussion: Overview, Rationale, and
  Structure
  o The City began the comprehensive environmental sustainability plan in
  2023 with federal funding support; ESA engaged; Principal Planner
  Shannon Wages presented.
  o Rationale: climate urgency (heat, air quality, water), equity, economic
  benefits, and community readiness; city should lead by example.
  o Plan vision with six core outcomes; three themes and nine sectors with
  goals, strategies, actions, targets, and baselines:
   Theme 1: Quality of life (green space, food, mobility,
  sustainability culture).
   Theme 2: Climate resilience (energy/buildings, water, air
  quality).
   Theme 3: Economic sustainability (green economy, waste
  reduction).
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Special Meeting on April 16, 2026

  o  Examples: food sector expansions; energy/buildings focusing on clean
  energy and efficiency (e.g., street lights); green economy job creation
  and sustainable business practices.
  o Community-facing infographics with household-level tips for renters,
  homeowners, and businesses.
  o Ongoing public review; ESA presenting high-level structure.
•  Community Engagement: Status, Concerns, and Planned Improvements
  o Engagement reached 700+ people via workshops, town halls, pop-ups,
  questionnaires; additional event engagement (e.g., Lunar New Year,
  eco fair) not fully quantified.
  o Current plan: public comment through April 30; finalize in May;
  council hearings/adoption targeted June–July; some participants
  requested extending feedback to 3–4 months with more town halls and
  weekly farmers market presence.
  o Concerns: document length and clarity; limited feedback window;
  reach (<10% of ~80,000 population) seen as insufficient; need for
  more frequent in-person opportunities and stronger language
  accessibility.
  o Staff emphasized ongoing, iterative engagement tied to CIP cycles; not
  the last chance for input; funding cycles will include recurring input
  opportunities.
  o Intent to partner with CBOs (Active SGV for canvassing, APIFM,
  Chinatown Service Center) for outreach and language support; need to
  make these partnerships explicit in the plan.
•  Accessibility, Translation, and Readability
  o “What can you do” pages praised for tangibility; noted typos and
  repetitive items; request for an easier-to-read summary and plain-
  language explanations of technical concepts (e.g., VMT, tree canopy).
  o Plan to develop a Sustainable Alhambra website and educational
  materials; translations planned in English, Spanish, Traditional
  Chinese; commitment to comprehensive edit and WCAG 2.1
  compliance (including color adjustments).
  o Workshop handouts are dense; request to display environmental,
  social/combined, and financial scores side-by-side for clearer
  prioritization and spending context.
  o Materials and programs currently not translated; recent workshop
  attendance was low; need to address translation and availability in
  multiple languages.
•  Implementation, Scoring, and Prioritization (Triple Bottom Line)
  o 175 actionable items with implementation tables (lead, supporting
  departments, timelines, cost comparisons).

  Page 2 of 5
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Special Meeting on April 16, 2026

  o  Scoring per action: environmental co-benefits (low to transformative),
  social impact (internal/limited to broad equity and community
  benefits), and financial cost (staff time/low to significant capital).
  o Combined environmental + social scores shown; financial scored
  separately; commission discussed prioritizing low-cost, high-benefit
  “low-hanging fruit.”
  o Example highlighted: coordinating land use and transportation to
  connect residential development with non-vehicle infrastructure and
  regional transit (high combined score, low cost).
  o Suggestions to categorize actions into short-, medium-, and long-term
  with scores and costs to reduce choice overload; proposal to start with
  top 20 by combined score, then select top 10 to advance with
  departments.
  o Clarification: public draft seeks “Did we miss anything?” rather than
  community ranking of 170+ actions at this stage; the commission may
  take a more active role in prioritization.
•  Equity and Renters’ Access
  o Approximately 60% of residents are renters; concern that unit-level
  improvements and voluntary programs may exclude renters lacking
  control over compost access and appliances.
  o Suggestions: incentives or requirements for developers to include
  public-accessible open/green spaces; consider density or parking
  reductions in exchange for public open space; review plan actions to
  ensure renter accessibility; note evolving opportunities (e.g., CPA heat
  pump offerings).
•  Commission Role, Council Expectations, and Timeline
  o Adoption viewed as a high-level endorsement to unlock funding;
  detailed implementation to follow over a five-year cycle.
  o Some commissioners are not ready to endorse without more outreach
  and detailed review; desire for additional meetings to refine sections
  (e.g., tree ordinance).
  o Council seeks confirmation the Commission is “on board” at a high
  level; aim to return to Council by end of June aligned with fiscal year
  start; budget constraints limit new outreach.
  o Proposal to extend the next meeting to review sections for gaps/misses;
  commissioners to bring 2–3 priority items on May 14; staff to compile
  section-by-section notes to transmit to City Council.
•  Community Program Alignment and Inter-Committee Coordination
  o Example: Buy Nothing activities at Alhambra Park faced
  reservations/fee barriers; plan actions (repair/reuse culture; donation
  programs) could address barriers and should be communicated to
  partners; no immediate resolution on park policy.

  Page 3 of 5
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Special Meeting on April 16, 2026

  o Transportation Committee engagement queried; staff noted alignment
  with existing mobility plans and ongoing stakeholder input; specific
  coordination mechanism not detailed.
  •  Upcoming City Environmental Events and Outreach
  o Arbor Day includes a tree planting; opportunity for commissioners to
  staff a booth at the Eco Fair.
  o Earth Day/Earth Fair scheduled for April 26, 2026 with environmental
  booths (stormwater, water quality, sustainability, recycling).
  o Neighborhood cleanup event planned; outreach materials distributed at
  city facilities (including library) and on the city website.
Public comment:
(Sawyer Brooks):
  • Commendations and critique; draft memo provided; review period short.
  o Plan focuses on voluntary programs; missing larger policies, funding,
  best practices; should include big levers requiring council approval.
  • Strengthen plan for renters, energy, and electrification; recognize CPA’s 100%
  green power.
  o Proposes renter/landlord support strategies; binding standards like
  building performance; electrify-on-replacement ordinances; immediate
  GHG reductions from electrification.
  • Stronger transportation policy and commission oversight; fund full 57-mile
  bike network; expand Commission mandate.
  o Adopt binding TDM ordinance; expand micromobility; aim to fund
  full bike network; Commission to actively oversee execution with
  measurable goals and reports; call for ambitious revisions before
  moving forward.
Commission Communication/Discussion:
  •  Distribute actionable item packets by theme to commissioners for review.
  •  Extend the next meeting duration to review each plan section for gaps or
  additions.
  •  Commissioners prepare 2–3 priority items to present at the May 14 meeting;
  consider survey/doodle to collect priorities.
  •  Staff compile section-by-section Commission notes into a transmittal to City
  Council.
  •  Hold a virtual workshop next week on the public draft; clarify and
  communicate additional engagement opportunities beyond April.
  •  Consider extending public comment period or adding town halls and regular
  farmers market presence.
  •  Prepare simplified, plain-language “What you can do” summary and
  explanatory materials; ensure WCAG 2.1 compliance.
  •  Provide multilingual materials (English, Spanish, Traditional Chinese);
  evaluate translation needs and quality; commissioners to review translations.

  Page 4 of 5
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Special Meeting on April 16, 2026

  •  Update workshop materials to show environmental, social/combined, and
  financial scores side-by-side.
  •  Make partnerships with Active SGV, APIFM, and Chinatown Service Center
  explicit in the plan and engagement process.
  •  Collaborate with NGOs/community partners to explain complex items and
  broaden feedback; provide approximate outreach reach with clear caveats.
  •  Develop a prioritization proposal (e.g., top 20 by combined score, then top 10
  to advance) and define the commission’s proactive role.
  •  Review park use policies affecting repair/reuse/donation activities and identify
  near-term fixes; communicate supportive measures to community partners.
  •  Coordinate with the Transportation Committee to ensure awareness and
  support of transportation-related actions.
  •  Identify funding and grant opportunities, including strategies to expand the
  Walk Bike Move network beyond 20 miles.
  •  Receive and review the final public comment memo from Sawyer Brooks;
  define process and timeline for considering revisions based on public
  comments.
  •  Confirm feasibility of returning the plan to City Council by end of June given
  budget constraints; align endorsement language and expectations.
  •  Coordinate commissioner participation at upcoming environmental events
  (Arbor Day, Eco Fair, Earth Fair on April 26, 2026).

Meeting Adjournment:
Meeting adjourned at 7:23 p.m.; closing remarks.
  • Motion to adjourn passed; staff thanks; attendees note sharing remarks with
  others; “Lots of good input.”

  MINUTES
  Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Meeting on May 14, 2026

The regular meeting of the Environmental Sustainability Commission was called to
order at 6:00 p.m. on May 14, 2026.

Roll Call
  Commission Members Present: Commissioner K. Chan, Commissioner Gomez,
  Commissioner Hermosillo, Commissioner Scaduto

  Staff Present: Latoya Waters – Deputy Director of Utilities serving as
  Commission Secretary, Lucy Garcia – Assistant City Manager, Katie Martel –
  Management Analyst: Sustainability.

  Members of the Public:
  None.

Meeting Minutes (Special Meeting) – April 16, 2026
    Approval of April 16, 2026 Meeting Minutes
  o Motion to approve was made and seconded (Commissioner Gomez
  moved; Commissioner Hermosillo seconded).
  o April 16, 2026 minutes approved.
Sustainability Plan Update:
   Comprehensive Sustainability Plan (Plan)
  o The public comment period for the environmental plan draft ended on
  April 30, with approximately 20 entities submitting feedback.
  o The consultant team is compiling comments into a matrix to be
  included as an appendix in the final plan.
  o Key themes from public feedback: a clearer implementation plan, a
  defined role for the commission, and more detail on monitoring and
  metrics.
  o The final draft will be strengthened—especially the plan’s purpose,
  alignment with other City plans, and a section addressing vulnerable
  communities, including renters.
  o Final Council approval and adoption are scheduled for the June 22
  Council meeting.
  o The staff report to Council will summarize public comments and
  amendments made to the draft.
  o The Plan is intended to be a living, flexible document that can be
  amended over time as priorities and technologies evolve.

    Budget and Funding for Sustainability Initiatives
  o City Council has allocated a one-time $160,000 to initiate climate and
  sustainability efforts.
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Meeting on May 14, 2026

  o  This seed funding will be leveraged with grants and partnerships to
  expand resources.
  o  A portion may support education, outreach, and materials.
  o  The Commission proposed establishing an annual sustainability budget
  line item (e.g., $250,000–$500,000 per year).
  o  The $160,000 is available to kick-start initiatives.
  o  The Commission will receive updates on spending and help steer its
  application.
  o  The City is actively pursuing grants; a comprehensive list of funding
  opportunities will be included in the plan.

Public comment:
(None)

Commission Communication/Discussion:
   Commissioners discussed submitting collective or individual
  recommendations to council before June 22.
   Priority areas identified:
  o Urban Forestry: Emphasize tree planting, strengthen the tree
  preservation ordinance, and develop an urban forest management plan.
  o Waste Reduction: Ban single-use plastics and expanded polystyrene;
  move from incentives to enforceable reductions.
  o Air Quality: Implement a phased ban on gas-powered leaf blowers;
  address pollution from major sources (freeways, railways).
  o Land Use: Maintain the ban on artificial turf, promote native
  landscaping, and explore community gardens on underutilized lots.
   Concerns include the rapid approval timeline and insufficient
  detail on metrics, goals, and actionable items.
   Stronger renter support is needed, especially for cooling
  measures due to rising heat.
   Funding Allocation and Implementation Timeline
  o The discussion opened with how to deploy the available $160,000 to
  deliver visible, public-facing results, especially tree planting.
  o The public wants to see more trees and is less concerned about process
  details.
  o The Commission needs clarity on what $160,000 can realistically
  accomplish; current plan line items show only dollar signs without cost
  detail.
  o One option is to treat the $160,000 as a revolving fund—modeled on a
  prior $200,000 tree-planting fund—to amplify its impact.
   Integrating New Initiatives with Existing Programs
  o A substantial share of funds could support education, outreach, and
  multilingual services, including translation and events.
  o New efforts, such as a green certification for restaurants, can be
  embedded within existing programs (e.g., the fats, oils, and grease
  inspection program) rather than launched as standalone initiatives.
  o Outreach for new environmental initiatives can ride along with current
  City outreach on stormwater, water conservation, and water quality.

  Page 2 of 4
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Meeting on May 14, 2026

  o  The objective is to avoid silos and weave new plan items into existing
  City programs for long-term sustainability.
   Commission's Role and Future Reporting
  o The Commission questioned its discretionary authority over the funds
  and asked that spending decisions come to them for pre-approval and
  input.
  o It was clarified that progress reports will go back to the council, and
  the Commission can make recommendations on the initial $160,000.
  o City departments were asked to present current projects, timelines, and
  approximate costs at the next commission meeting to identify where
  the new plan fits.
  o The Commission also requested a Capital Improvement Program (CIP)
  overview to understand upcoming projects aligned with sustainability
  goals.
   Formal Recommendation to City Council
  o The Commission agreed to prepare and submit a formal letter or memo
  with combined recommendations to the City Council before the June
  22nd meeting.
  o Submission is requested within the next one to two weeks.
   Story Park Project Update
  o The Commission inquired about the Story Park project, which is seeking
  design funding from the Safe Clean Water Program.
  o Staff reported, the outlook is positive: competing projects are larger,
  and one (Pasadena) is pursuing alternative funding, freeing up funds.
  o Public call-ins supporting Story Park were highly impactful;
  commissioners were asked to call in again for the next Watershed Area
  Steering Committee (WASC) meeting.
   Tree Removal and Ordinance Enforcement
  o The Commissioners raised serious concern about the removal of many
  large, mature trees for a new storage facility on Meridian.
  o The incident underscores the need to strengthen the City’s tree
  ordinance and improve coordination among commissions and
  departments (e.g., the building department).
  o The Commission emphasized holding developers accountable with
  more than fines—e.g., making building permits contingent on
  compliance with tree preservation rules.
  o The Commission resolved to recommend that the council direct the
  city attorney to draft a stronger tree ordinance within 90–120 days.
Action Items:
  o Staff:
   Provide current projects, timelines, and approximate costs,
  organized by the plan’s nine sectors.
   Compile a list of grant opportunities as part of the Plan’s
  funding strategy.
   Share updated call-in information for the next Watershed Area
  Steering Committee (WASC) meeting to support the Story Park
  Project.
  o Commission:

  Page 3 of 4
   MINUTES
  Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Meeting on May 14, 2026

    Draft and finalize a letter with the Commission’s
  recommendations for the City Council; submit within 1–2
  weeks.
    Submit a formal recommendation to the City Council
  requesting that the city attorney draft a stronger tree ordinance
  within 90–120 days.

Meeting Adjournment:
Meeting adjourned at 7:10 p.m.; closing remarks.
   Motion to adjourn passed.
